claim: Visual and olfactory associative memories of Drosophila share mushroom body (MB) circuits.
source: Previously, we demonstrated that visual and olfactory associative memories of Drosophila share mushroom body (MB) circuits (Vogt et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to previous work (Vogt et al., 2014).

claim: A small subset of MB Kenyon cells (KCs) selectively responds to visual but not olfactory stimulation.
source: Here, we show that a small subset of MB Kenyon cells (KCs) selectively responds to visual but not olfactory stimulation.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript, including electrophysiological recordings shown in Figure 2E,G.

claim: The dendrites of atypical KCs form a ventral accessory calyx (vAC), distinct from the main calyx that receives olfactory input.
source: The dendrites of these atypical KCs form a ventral accessory calyx (vAC), distinct from the main calyx that receives olfactory input.
evidence: The claim is supported by anatomical data and imaging shown in Figures 1B and 2B.

claim: Two types of visual projection neurons (VPNs) directly connect the optic lobes and the vAC.
source: We identified two types of visual projection neurons (VPNs) directly connecting the optic lobes and the vAC.
evidence: The claim is supported by anatomical screening and imaging data shown in Figure 3.

claim: VPNs are differentially required for visual memories of color and brightness.
source: Strikingly, these VPNs are differentially required for visual memories of color and brightness.
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral experiments shown in Figure 4B,C,E,F demonstrating differential requirements for VPN-MB1 and VPN-MB2.

claim: The segregation of visual and olfactory domains in the MB allows independent processing of distinct sensory memories.
source: The segregation of visual and olfactory domains in the MB allows independent processing of distinct sensory memories and may be a conserved form of sensory representations among insects.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data showing modality segregation and comparison with other insects.

claim: The mushroom body (MB) receives distinct dopaminergic inputs that signal reward and punishment.
source: In the fruit fly, the MB receives distinct dopaminergic inputs that signal reward and punishment, and this valence circuit in the MB is shared for associative memories of different modalities: olfaction, gustation, and vision (Masek et al., 2015; Aso et al., 2012; Liu et al., 2012; Perisse et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: The role of MB output during memory acquisition and testing is similar in visual and olfactory memories.
source: The role of MB output during memory acquisition and testing is similar in visual and olfactory memories (Vogt et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The required subsets of MB Kenyon cells (KCs) are not the same for visual and olfactory memories.
source: However, the required subsets of MB Kenyon cells (KCs) are not the same (Aso et al., 2014a; Vogt et al., 2014), raising the possibility that memory-relevant visual and olfactory information may be represented by different KC subsets in the MB.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: MBs of hymenoptera receive visual afferents in their calyces.
source: MBs of hymenoptera receive visual afferents in their calyces (Ehmer and Gronenberg, 2002; Gronenberg and Hölldobler, 1999; Paulk and Gronenberg, 2008), while such direct visual input from the optic lobes to the MBs has never been observed in dipteran insects (Mu et al., 2012; Otsuna and Ito, 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: Direct visual input from the optic lobes to the MBs has never been observed in dipteran insects.
source: MBs of hymenoptera receive visual afferents in their calyces (Ehmer and Gronenberg, 2002; Gronenberg and Hölldobler, 1999; Paulk and Gronenberg, 2008), while such direct visual input from the optic lobes to the MBs has never been observed in dipteran insects (Mu et al., 2012; Otsuna and Ito, 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Indirect, multisynaptic pathways have been proposed to convey the visual input to the Drosophila MB.
source: Therefore, indirect, multisynaptic pathways have been proposed to convey the visual input to the Drosophila MB (Farris and Van Dyke, 2015; Tanaka et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Memory was consistently impaired when drivers labelling the γ-lobe neurons were used.
source: Memory was consistently impaired when we used drivers labelling the γ-lobe neurons, confirming their importance for visual memory (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) (Vogt et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and cited previous work.

claim: A subset of the γ neurons (γd) is specifically responsible for visual memory.
source: Strikingly, this screen further suggested a subset of the γ neurons (γd) to be specifically responsible (Figure 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral screening data shown in Figure 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The γd neurons are embryonic born KCs consisting of ca. 75 cells in the adult brain.
source: The γd neurons are embryonic born KCs consisting of ca. 75 cells in the adult brain (Butcher et al., 2012; Aso et al., 2009; Aso et al., 2014b).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Two split-GAL4 drivers MB607B and MB419B showed strong expression in the γd neurons but had no detectable expression in other KCs.
source: Two split-GAL4 drivers MB607B and MB419B showed strong expression in the γd neurons but had no detectable expression in other KCs (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The blockade of the γd neurons using MB607B and MB419B lines severely impaired visual memory.
source: The blockade of the γd neurons using these lines severely impaired visual memory (Figure 1D,E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 1D,E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Olfactory memory of flies with γd neuron blockade was not significantly affected.
source: In contrast, olfactory memory of these flies was not significantly affected (Figure 1F, Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The selective γd requirement for visual memory suggests that these KCs represent visual stimuli.
source: Given that both visual and olfactory memories were reinforced by the same aversive stimulus - electric shock punishment - the selective γd requirement for visual memory suggests that these KCs represent visual stimuli.
evidence: The claim is based on logical inference from the experimental results showing selective impairment of visual but not olfactory memory.

claim: γd cell axons run in parallel to those of the other KCs in the peduncle, and project to the dorsomedial tip of the γd lobe.
source: Their axons run in parallel to those of the other KCs in the peduncle, and project to the dorsomedial tip of the γd lobe (Figure 1B, 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by anatomical imaging data shown in Figure 1B and 2A.

claim: The γd neurons are atypical in that their dendrites are highly enriched ventrolaterally outside the main calyx, where olfactory projection neurons (OPNs) terminate.
source: The γd neurons are atypical in that their dendrites are highly enriched ventrolaterally outside the main calyx, where olfactory projection neurons (OPNs) terminate (Figure 1B, 2B), and form the ventral accessory calyx (vAC) (Butcher et al., 2012; Aso et al., 2014b).
evidence: The claim is supported by anatomical imaging data shown in Figure 1B and 2B, and citations to previous studies.

claim: The γd neurons are equipped with claw-like dendritic endings forming microglomeruli similar to those in the main calyx.
source: Nevertheless, the γd neurons are equipped with claw-like dendritic endings forming microglomeruli similar to those in the main calyx (Figure 2C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by high-resolution imaging data shown in Figure 2C,D.

claim: Some γd cells showed spiking responses to blue and green light stimuli.
source: In line with the specific requirement of γd neurons for visual conditioning, we found spiking responses to blue and green light stimuli in some of these cells (Figure 2E,G).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological recording data shown in Figure 2E,G.

claim: Stimulating flies with 5 different odors did not lead to excitatory responses of the γd neurons.
source: Stimulating flies with 5 different odors did not lead to excitatory responses of the γd neurons; olfactory stimulation rather evoked slow inhibitory responses, implying the existence of feedforward inhibition through other odor-responsive KC populations (Figure 2E,G).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological recording data shown in Figure 2E,G.

claim: Olfactory stimulation of γd neurons evoked slow inhibitory responses, implying the existence of feedforward inhibition through other odor-responsive KC populations.
source: Stimulating flies with 5 different odors did not lead to excitatory responses of the γd neurons; olfactory stimulation rather evoked slow inhibitory responses, implying the existence of feedforward inhibition through other odor-responsive KC populations (Figure 2E,G).
evidence: The claim involves inference from the observed inhibitory responses to explain the mechanism.

claim: The response profile of γd neurons is in sharp contrast to typical KCs (e.g. α/β neurons), many of which responded to odors but none to visual stimuli.
source: This response profile is in sharp contrast to what we observed with typical KCs (e.g. α/β neurons), many of which responded to odors but none to visual stimuli (Figure 2F,G, [Turner et al., 2008]).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological data shown in Figure 2F,G and a citation to previous work.

claim: There is clear modality segregation between γd and α/β neurons.
source: Thus, there is clear modality segregation between γd and α/β neurons.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the differential response profiles of γd and α/β neurons to visual and olfactory stimuli.

claim: Two types of neurons with arbors in the optic lobes and projections in the area of the vAC were identified as candidates for visual projection neurons (VPNs) to the MB.
source: Performing an anatomical screen of a GAL4 driver collection (Jenett et al., 2012), we identified two types of neurons with arbors in the optic lobes and projections in the area of the vAC, making them candidates for visual projection neurons (VPNs) to the MB (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by anatomical screening data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1 and a citation to the GAL4 collection.

claim: The two types of VPNs were named VPN-MB1 and VPN-MB2.
source: We named these two types of VPNs VPN-MB1 and VPN-MB2.
evidence: This is a direct statement of nomenclature used in the study.

claim: Split-GAL4 drivers MB425B and MB334C have strong expression in VPN-MB1 and VPN-MB2 with little other expression.
source: To precisely map the morphology of these VPNs, we generated split-GAL4 drivers, MB425B and MB334C. These drivers have strong expression in VPN-MB1 and VPN-MB2 with little other expression (Figure 3A,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3A,C.

claim: MB425B-GAL4 has predominant expression in VPN-MB1 projecting from the medulla to the vAC with many cell bodies on the anterior surface of the optic lobe.
source: MB425B-GAL4 has predominant expression in VPN-MB1 (Figure 3B) projecting from the medulla to the vAC with many cell bodies on the anterior surface of the optic lobe.
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: MB334C-GAL4 strongly labels 1–3 cells of VPN-MB2 as well as the MB output neurons MBON-α1.
source: In contrast, MB334C-GAL4 strongly labels 1–3 cells of VPN-MB2 as well as the MB output neurons MBON-α1 (Figure 3C,D) (Aso et al., 2014a; 2014b).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3C,D and citations to previous studies.

claim: The majority of VPN-MB1 and VPN-MB2 dendrites are localized to the optic lobes.
source: We found that the majority of VPN-MB1 and VPN-MB2 dendrites are localized to the optic lobes (Figure 3E,G).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3E,G.

claim: The VPN-MB1 neurons have dendritic arbors in the medulla enriched in layer M8.
source: The VPN-MB1 neurons have dendritic arbors in the medulla enriched in layer M8 (Figure 3F).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: VPN-MB1 neurons cover a large field of the medulla with a conspicuous elaboration in the ventral half.
source: They cover a large field of the medulla with a conspicuous elaboration in the ventral half (Figure 3A,E,F).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3A,E,F.

claim: Each VPN-MB1 cell samples input from approximately 20 optic cartridges in the medulla.
source: Single-cell labeling revealed that each VPN-MB1 cell samples input from approximately 20 optic cartridges in the medulla (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by single-cell labeling data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Dendrites of a single VPN-MB2 cover a large field of the ventral medulla, arborizing in layer M7.
source: Dendrites of a single VPN-MB2 cover a large field of the ventral medulla, arborizing in layer M7 (Figure 3C,D,G,H).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3C,D,G,H.

claim: The output sites of both VPNs are restricted to the lateral protocerebrum, including the vAC, forming pre-synaptic boutons in microglomeruli.
source: The output sites of both VPNs are restricted to the lateral protocerebrum, including the vAC, forming pre-synaptic boutons in microglomeruli (Figure 3E,G; Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3E,G and Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: The VPN terminals are enwrapped by the dendrites of the γd neurons.
source: To visualize possible connections between the VPNs and KCs in the vAC, we performed counterstaining of VPNs and the catalytic subunit of PKA that marks KCs (Wolff and Strausfeld, 2015) and found that the VPN terminals are enwrapped by the dendrites of the γd neurons (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2 and a citation.

claim: A GRASP signal was detected between the VPNs and the ventrolateral projection of the γd dendrites.
source: We also detected a GRASP signal between the VPNs and the ventrolateral projection of the γd dendrites (Figure 3I–L).
evidence: The claim is supported by GRASP imaging data shown in Figure 3I–L.

claim: Memory was not significantly altered upon the blockade of the OPNs.
source: Memory was not significantly altered upon the blockade of the OPNs (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The blockade of VPN-MB1, but not VPN-MB2, significantly impaired color discrimination memory.
source: In contrast, the blockade of VPN-MB1, but not VPN-MB2, significantly impaired color discrimination memory (Figure 4B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 4B,C.

claim: The blockade of VPNs in VT008475 that do not reach the vAC left color discrimination memory intact.
source: To further substantiate the results with MB425B-GAL4, we employed another driver line (VT008475) that labels similar VPNs to VPN-MB1. These VPNs in VT008475 project to the lateral protocerebrum but do not reach the vAC (Figure 4—figure supplement 1). The blockade of these VPNs left color discrimination memory intact (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral and imaging data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: VPN-MB1 is a key component of the visual learning pathway.
source: These results strongly suggest the existence of modality-specific input pathways to the MB and that VPN-MB1 is a key component of the visual learning pathway.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the behavioral and anatomical data showing VPN-MB1's requirement for color memory and its connection to the vAC.

claim: The γd neurons were necessary for brightness discrimination learning.
source: We asked if the γd neurons and same VPNs are also required for brightness discrimination learning. We found that while the γd neurons were also necessary for this task, the blockade of VPN-MB1 did not significantly alter performance (Figure 4D,E).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The blockade of VPN-MB1 did not significantly alter brightness discrimination learning performance.
source: We found that while the γd neurons were also necessary for this task, the blockade of VPN-MB1 did not significantly alter performance (Figure 4D,E).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Learning was significantly impaired by blockade of VPN-MB2 in brightness discrimination.
source: In contrast, learning was significantly impaired by blockade of VPN-MB2 (Figure 4F).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: The blockade of MBON-α1 did not significantly impair brightness discrimination learning.
source: Because MB334C-GAL4 has expression not just in VPN-MB2 but also in MBON-α1, we tested and ruled out the involvement of MBON-α1 by showing that its blockade did not significantly impair brightness discrimination learning (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: The differential requirements for VPN-MB1 and VPN-MB2 indicate that information about color and intensity of a visual cue is separately conveyed to the MB via distinct VPNs.
source: The differential requirements for VPN-MB1 and VPN-MB2 indicate that information about color and intensity of a visual cue is separately conveyed to the MB via distinct VPNs.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the differential behavioral requirements of VPN-MB1 and VPN-MB2 for color versus brightness discrimination.

claim: The MB had been thought to receive visual input from the optic lobe through an unknown indirect pathway, because direct connections had not been observed.
source: Previous studies have shown the importance of MB circuits for visual memories and other visually guided behaviors in Drosophila (Vogt et al., 2014; Liu et al., 1999; Zhang et al., 2007); however, the MB had been thought to receive visual input from the optic lobe through an unknown indirect pathway, because direct connections had not been observed (Farris and Van Dyke, 2015; Tanaka et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The identification of direct pathways reveals similarity between dipteran and hymenopteran circuit design for visual processing.
source: Our identification of direct pathways reveals similarity between dipteran and hymenopteran circuit design for visual processing, and provides experimental evidence for the behavioral roles of these circuits (Figure 4G).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the current findings and comparison with known hymenopteran circuits.

claim: VPN-MB1 and VPN-MB2 receive differential inputs in the medulla and convey distinct visual features - color and brightness - to the MB.
source: VPN-MB1 and VPN-MB2 receive differential inputs in the medulla and convey distinct visual features - color and brightness - to the MB.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the anatomical localization and behavioral requirements of the two VPN types.

claim: The medulla layer M8 where VPN-MB1 arborizes contains presynaptic terminals of Tm5 neurons that are involved in color vision.
source: The medulla layer M8 where VPN-MB1 arborizes (Figure 3F) contains presynaptic terminals of Tm5 neurons that are involved in color vision (Karuppudurai et al., 2014; Gao et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by anatomical data shown in Figure 3F and citations to previous studies.

claim: VPN-MB2 is the first Drosophila interneuron shown to convey brightness information.
source: VPN-MB2 is the first Drosophila interneuron shown to convey brightness information, and the position of its dendrites suggests that light intensity may be encoded in the medulla layer M7 (Figure 3H).
evidence: The claim is based on the behavioral requirement of VPN-MB2 for brightness discrimination and its anatomical localization.

claim: The position of VPN-MB2 dendrites suggests that light intensity may be encoded in the medulla layer M7.
source: VPN-MB2 is the first Drosophila interneuron shown to convey brightness information, and the position of its dendrites suggests that light intensity may be encoded in the medulla layer M7 (Figure 3H).
evidence: The claim is speculative, based on the anatomical position of VPN-MB2 dendrites and its functional role.

claim: The dendrites of VPN-MB1 and VPN-MB2 are preferentially distributed in the ventral half of the medulla.
source: Interestingly, the dendrites of VPN-MB1 and VPN-MB2 are preferentially distributed in the ventral half of the medulla, an arrangement consistent with the specialization of the ventral retina for color processing of landmarks during foraging (Giger and Srinivasan, 1997; Kinoshita et al., 2015; Wernet et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by anatomical observations and citations to previous studies on retinal specialization.

claim: The target region of the MB-projecting VPNs is separated from other described VPNs in the central brain.
source: The target region of the MB-projecting VPNs is separated from other described VPNs in the central brain, and largely segregated from other VPNs mediating innate spectral processing and motion vision (Mu et al., 2012; Otsuna and Ito, 2006; Zhang et al., 2013a).
evidence: The claim is supported by anatomical observations and citations to previous studies.

claim: Parallel processing of different visual features with segregated projections may be a conserved circuit strategy for visual processing across phyla.
source: Parallel processing of different visual features with segregated projections may be a conserved circuit strategy for visual processing across phyla (Livingstone and Hubel, 1988).
evidence: The claim is speculative, drawing on comparison with other systems and citing previous work.

claim: The Drosophila MB represents distinct sensory modalities in different KC subsets whose dendrites are segregated in subdomains of the calyx.
source: Our results provide evidence that the Drosophila MB represents distinct sensory modalities in different KC subsets whose dendrites are segregated in subdomains of the calyx.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data showing modality-specific KC responses and anatomical segregation.

claim: Olfactory inputs project to the main calyx and visual stimuli to the vAC.
source: Olfactory inputs project to the main calyx and visual stimuli to the vAC, while gustatory stimuli have been recently shown to project to yet another calyx domain (Kirkhart and Scott, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by the current study's data and a citation to previous work on gustatory inputs.

claim: Gustatory stimuli have been recently shown to project to yet another calyx domain.
source: Olfactory inputs project to the main calyx and visual stimuli to the vAC, while gustatory stimuli have been recently shown to project to yet another calyx domain (Kirkhart and Scott, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Dopamine neurons including those encoding positive and negative valences divide the long axon terminals of KCs into distinct compartments.
source: In the fly MB, dopamine neurons including those encoding positive and negative valences divide the long axon terminals of KCs into distinct compartments (Aso et al., 2014a; Tanaka et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: A single dopamine neuron locally modulates the corresponding axonal compartment of multiple KCs.
source: As KCs send parallel axon fibers, a single dopamine neuron locally modulates the corresponding axonal compartment of multiple KCs (Hige et al., 2015; Cohn et al., 2016; Boto et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Distinct KC subsets, γd and γm for example, can share the same dopaminergic valence modulation, even if these KCs are devoted to different sensory modalities.
source: Distinct KC subsets, γd and γm for example, can therefore share the same dopaminergic valence modulation, even if these KCs are devoted to different sensory modalities (Figure 4G) (Vogt et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the circuit architecture and cited previous work.

claim: Local modulations in KC axonal compartments affect the information conveyed by shared MB output pathways.
source: These local modulations in turn affect the information conveyed by shared MB output pathways (Figure 4G) (Aso et al., 2014; Vogt et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the circuit architecture and cited previous work.

claim: There appears to be a close correlation between the ecological specialization of different insects and the organization of their MB calyces.
source: There appears to be a close correlation between the ecological specialization of different insects and the organization of their MB calyces (Ehmer and Gronenberg, 2002; Lin and Strausfeld, 2012; Yilmaz et al., 2016; Groh et al., 2014), with the functional subdivision of the calyx reflecting the salient sensory environment.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous comparative studies.

claim: Olfactory processing utilizes ~1800 of the 2000 KCs in Drosophila.
source: Olfactory processing, which is the dominant sensory modality in Drosophila subject to associative modulation, utilizes ~1800 of the 2000 KCs (Quinn et al., 1974).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: While fruit flies perform a wide range of behaviors driven by visual input, few could be modified by associative learning.
source: While fruit flies perform a wide range of behaviors driven by visual input, few could be modified by associative learning (Borst, 2009), given that fewer KCs subserve visual memory formation.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation and inference from the number of KCs devoted to visual processing.

claim: The MB calyces of other insects possess modality segregation, and different sets of KCs are presumably assigned to each sensory space.
source: The MB calyces of other insects also possess modality segregation, and different sets of KCs are presumably assigned to each sensory space (Gronenberg and Hölldobler, 1999; Kinoshita et al., 2015; Mobbs, 1982).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies and involves speculation about KC assignment.

claim: The current results are the first to show that individual KCs have unimodal responses.
source: Our results here are the first to show that individual KCs indeed have unimodal responses.
evidence: The claim is based on the electrophysiological data showing modality-specific responses in γd versus α/β KCs.

claim: The segregated sensory representation in the MB enables independent formation of different sensory memories.
source: The segregated sensory representation in the MB enables independent formation of different sensory memories, while allowing interaction among distinct KC populations that may underlie complex forms of learning involving multimodal integration (Zhang et al., 2013b).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the segregated architecture and cited previous work on multimodal integration.

claim: Interaction among distinct KC populations may underlie complex forms of learning involving multimodal integration.
source: The segregated sensory representation in the MB enables independent formation of different sensory memories, while allowing interaction among distinct KC populations that may underlie complex forms of learning involving multimodal integration (Zhang et al., 2013b).
evidence: The claim is speculative, suggesting a possible mechanism for multimodal learning, supported by a citation.

claim: Flies were reared at 25°C, at 60% relative humidity under a 12-12-hr light-dark cycle on a standard cornmeal-based diet.
source: Flies were reared at 25°C, at 60% relative humidity under a 12-12-hr light-dark cycle on a standard cornmeal-based diet.
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing experimental conditions.

claim: Each behavioral experiment used 30–40 flies of mixed gender under dim red light.
source: Each behavioral experiment used 30–40 flies of mixed gender under dim red light in a custom-made plastic box, containing a heating element on the bottom and a fan for air circulation.
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing experimental conditions.

claim: The intensities of blue and green LEDs were 19.4 mW/m2 and 8.58 mW/m2 respectively.
source: The intensities were controlled by current and calibrated using a luminance meter BM-9 (Topcon Technohouse Corporation) or a PR-655 SpectraScan Spectroradiometer: 19.4 mW/m2 (blue) and 8.58 mW/m2 (green) (Schnaitmann et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing stimulus parameters.

claim: To train flies with different light intensities, blue and green visual cues were replaced by different intensities of green light (1:10 ratio; 27.8 mW/m2 (bright-green), and 2.77 mW/m2 (dark-green).
source: To train flies with different light intensities, blue and green visual cues were replaced by different intensities of green light (1:10 ratio; 27.8 mW/m2 (bright-green), and 2.77 mW/m2 (dark-green).
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing stimulus parameters.

claim: During training, a 1-s electric shock (AC 60 V) was applied 12 times spaced over 60 s during presentation of the punished visual stimulus.
source: During a training trial, the entire arena was illuminated with alternating visual stimuli (60 s each) with one stimulus paired with aversive reinforcement. A 1-s electric shock (AC 60 V) was applied 12 times spaced over 60 s during presentation of the punished visual stimulus.
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing training protocol.

claim: The whole experimental setup was kept at 33°C for the temperature-induced effect of Shits1.
source: The whole experimental setup was kept at 33°C for the temperature-induced effect of Shits1.
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing experimental conditions.

claim: OCT and MCH were diluted to 0.6% and 2%, respectively, in paraffin oil for olfactory conditioning.
source: OCT and MCH were diluted to 0.6% and 2%, respectively, in paraffin oil (Sigma-Aldrich) and presented in a cup with a diameter of 30 mm.
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing stimulus preparation.

claim: Twelve 1.5 s 90 V electric shocks (DC) were paired with one of the odor presentations during olfactory conditioning.
source: Twelve 1.5 s 90 V electric shocks (DC) were paired with one of the odor presentations.
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing training protocol.

claim: The distributions of all four response categories are significantly different between γd KCs and α/β KCs with respect to both visual (p<10–5, Fisher's exact test) and odor responses (p<10–6).
source: The distributions of all four response categories are significantly different between γd KCs and α/β KCs with respect to both visual (p<10–5, Fisher's exact test) and odor responses (p<10–6)
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical analysis of electrophysiological data.

claim: Split-GAL4 line MB425B carries 28F07-p65ADZp in attP40 and 10E05-ZpGdbd in attP2.
source: Split-GAL4 lines were generated using described vectors (Pfeiffer et al., 2010): MB425B carries 28F07-p65ADZp in attP40 and 10E05-ZpGdbd in attP2, MB334C carries 52G04-p65ADZp in attP40 and 49F03-ZpGdbd in VK00027.
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing genetic constructs.

claim: Split-GAL4 line MB334C carries 52G04-p65ADZp in attP40 and 49F03-ZpGdbd in VK00027.
source: Split-GAL4 lines were generated using described vectors (Pfeiffer et al., 2010): MB425B carries 28F07-p65ADZp in attP40 and 10E05-ZpGdbd in attP2, MB334C carries 52G04-p65ADZp in attP40 and 49F03-ZpGdbd in VK00027.
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing genetic constructs.
